records.region: Côte d'Ivoire (Abidjan), Ethiopia (Addis Ababa), Switzerland (Geneva) - host institutions for nationals of any African country
records.duration: 12 months

records.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.
records.best_fit: African nationals with a master's degree and at least seven years of relevant work experience who want senior-level policy exposure in a continental or multilateral institution.
records.eligibility_summary: Nationals of any African country with a minimum master's degree, at least seven years of relevant work experience, and under 40 (45 for women with children).

Minimum 7 years' of relevant work experience

Under the age of 40; or 45 for women with children

coverage: Annual stipend (Foundation states $100,000), paid monthly by the host institution
Foundation-funded travel and shipping costs for assumption of duty and repatriation

benefits: Membership of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation's Now Generation Network (NGN) after the Fellowship
requirements: Apply online through the host organisation's own application system
Submit a comprehensive Curriculum Vitae indicating date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience

application_method: Choose the host organisation route on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page
Open the host organisation's vacancy or programme page (AfDB, ITC or UNECA)
Complete the online application form on the host's system
Attach CV, academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation before the host's closing date
records.selection_notes: The host's Human Resources department vets applications to draw up a shortlist of ten files, which the Foundation then reviews; a shortlist of three candidates is put to the head of the host (for the AfDB route, the President of the Bank or a designate) for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted.
records.notes: This is a work placement, not a degree programme: the contract is for one (1) year and is not renewable, and the Fellow is not a regular employee of the host and gains no right to employment. For the AfDB route the Fellow is barred from applying for a staff position at the Bank for one year from the end of the Fellowship. The Fellow is not eligible for the Bank's child educational scheme, staff medical insurance or retirement plans; the Mo Ibrahim Foundation is responsible for ensuring the Fellow arranges their own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan. Applications are routed through three different host systems with potentially different closing dates, so check the host page you intend to use.

records.name: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship (Class of 2028)
records.region: South Africa (study must be in South Africa) - for citizens of any African country
records.duration: Maximum two years of funding; one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Masters
records.deadline: Applications for 2028 will open 9 March 2027. Applications close by the end of Wednesday, 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.application_period: The applications timeline runs from March to November of each year for the following year's intake. For the Class of 2028: applications open Tuesday 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship funds a one-year Honours degree or a two-year Masters degree in any field at a recognised South African institution of higher education, and pairs it with a compulsory Leadership Development Programme of residential workshops and regional pods. The Foundation states it offers comprehensive funding for the core costs of study: tuition and registration fees, a study materials allowance, research and conferencing grants on request, a medical aid allowance, accommodation and meal allowances, a personal allowance, and economy-class flights between the scholar's home country and their South African institution at the start and end of the degree. The Foundation does not pay university application fees, SAQA accreditation of existing degrees, or visa application costs. Specific allowance amounts are set by the Foundation and no figures are published.
records.program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship with leadership development programme
records.best_fit: African citizens aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree above 70% or an upper-second class Honours, who intend to study an Honours or Masters degree in South Africa and can commit to the compulsory leadership programme.
records.eligibility_summary: Citizen of an African country, aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree completed by 1 January 2028 with above 70% or upper-second class results, and able to study at postgraduate level in English.

I admire Nelson Mandela's ability to bridge divides and bring people together around our common humanity
I am prepared to reflect deeply on my own leadership and undergo a process of personal change and growth

records.selection_notes: The Foundation looks for young leaders who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, and who demonstrate the combination of intellect and character. Applicants are screened in rounds: a notification by mid-July indicates whether the applicant reached Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, and by end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.
records.notes: The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered. Attendance at the residential workshops and regional pods is mandatory and a condition of the scholarship, and the Foundation will not accept travel outside South Africa, even for research purposes, as a reason for absence. You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities and may not do paid work for more than 12 hours a week. The award is conditional on you being offered a place at a South African institution, and the Foundation does not apply to universities for you. If you are not accepted by a South African institution in time, you cannot accept the scholarship. The Foundation does not pay visa application costs, and states that a delayed visa may mean you cannot start on time and could lose the scholarship. Applicants from outside South Africa may need SAQA verification, which the Foundation states can take 4-8 weeks and is not covered by the award. Any amount you owe prior to becoming a Scholar is your sole responsibility. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, block courses, or courses delivered predominantly online, and distance learning is not allowed.

records.name: TEF Entrepreneurship Programme
records.degree_levels: Not a degree programme (entrepreneurship training and seed funding)
records.region: All 54 African countries - applicants must reside in Africa and establish their business in Africa
records.duration: Annual cohort cycle: application, due diligence, shortlist, training, investment readiness, then seed capital disbursement
records.deadline: Every year, the application portal for our flagship TEF Entrepreneurship Programme opens on the 1st of January till midnight on the 1st of March at Midnight, on our digital platform, www.TEFConnect.com.
records.application_period: The application window opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March each year, for that year's cohort. The next published window after 2026-10-01 is 1 January 2027 to midnight 1 March 2027.
records.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. This is a business grant and training programme, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.
records.program_type: Foundation entrepreneurship grant and training programme
records.best_fit: Africans aged 18 and above who live in Africa, have a business idea or a business no older than five years, plan to build the business in Africa, and have never received a TEF programme award.
records.eligibility_summary: Africans aged 18 and above who reside in Africa, hold a business idea or a business no older than five years, plan to establish the business in Africa, and have never previously received any TEF programme or previously applied in the same application window of the same year.

records.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.
records.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.

official_details.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. records.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program enables highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and is delivered through partner universities and non-governmental organisations rather than through a single central application. Financial support includes tuition fees, accommodation, books and other academic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development, and a return air ticket to the Scholar's country of origin if necessary, alongside psychosocial and academic support. Admission to a partner institution does not guarantee selection for the scholarship.

records.notes: There is no central application, no central deadline and no central eligibility test, so a record of this scholarship cannot tell you whether a specific window is open. You must check each partner institution's own programme page for its deadline. Many partners require an admission application fee that the Foundation states will be reimbursed if you are selected, so do not let the fee stop you applying. The Foundation warns publicly that there are Facebook posts and groups advertising recruitment for this programme and requesting an application fee, and states that these groups are not associated with the Mastercard Foundation; the Foundation does not solicit funding or request payments from individuals. Report suspected fraud to local law enforcement and to ethics@mastercardfdn.org. PhD and doctoral candidates are not currently eligible. The Foundation does not provide financial support to candidates who are not awarded a scholarship through this programme. The Foundation is not currently accepting unsolicited partnership proposals.

records.description: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement is a two-year, non-degree award from the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation that lets young Indians pursue self-directed work on an issue of public importance under a mentor of their choice. award_holder_conditions: The scholarship is not repayable: 'Das Stipendium muss nicht zurückgezahlt werden.'

purpose: Support international students at a German higher education institution during their studies, materially and ideologically: 'Mit dem FES-Stipendium möchten wir Studierende während ihres Studiums unterstützen - materiell und ideell.'

Enable scholarship holders to concentrate on their studies without financial worries and to have more time for their civic engagement: 'Wir tragen dazu bei, dass unsere Stipendiat:innen sich ohne finanzielle Sorgen auf das Studium konzentrieren können und mehr Zeit für ihr Engagement haben.'
Give international students the chance to complete their studies at a German university. The Foundation states it is particularly pleased when it can give students from abroad that opportunity.

Promote education equity: 'Bildungsgerechtigkeit bedeutet gleiche Chancen für alle.' Selection gives particular weight to applications from people who are the first in their family to study (Erst-Akademiker:innen) and/or have a migration background, from women, and from students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects.

Cultivate a values-oriented environment in which holders exchange ideas and become able to gather sufficient information, act thoughtfully, make decisions and thereby strengthen their social participation.
The Foundation is convinced that commitment to society works best when achieved together.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published. The Foundation states its own commitment to the fundamental values of social democracy and asks applicants to identify with those values, which is a political-values test rather than a development-goal test.

Where the Foundation's stipend is described, it is described as support for living during the study, not as a fee waiver.

An additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children (stated on the German Grundförderung page)

host_requirements: The applicant must already be enrolled at a German public or state-recognised university, higher education institution or university of applied sciences (an einer deutschen, staatlichen oder staatlich anerkannten Hochschule oder Fachhochschule).
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and university entrance qualification and certificates are among the documents requested at the second stage.
The applicant's study must be a full-time degree programme; extra-occupational and part-time courses of study are not funded.
Scholarship holders with children receive an additional monthly amount, which requires a declared family situation.
The Foundation's English page notes particular importance for students at universities of applied sciences, so those institutions are an accepted host type rather than a second-tier route.
document_format_rules: The application is made in the online application form, using the form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A. The online form is required as the first step and is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria.

The first-step online form requires general personal information, information on professional and family background, the applicant's motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and information on socio-political engagement.
Applications must be submitted in German.

Second-stage documents requested by email: a detailed CV covering previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) and other evidence; a detailed letter of motivation; and two references (Gutachten) from university lecturers, or from teachers for first-year students.

For the Grundförderung, the Foundation publishes a dedicated document and reference checklist as a downloadable file at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624, which is the governing list of required documents and guidance for this programme specifically.
Applicants have three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, and the Foundation sends a receipt confirmation on receipt.

If an applicant is invited to a selection interview and has incurred travel costs, those costs can be reimbursed by submitting the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung (Fahrtkostenerstattung_BMFTR_Grundförderung), published at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=165947.
Applicants can log back in at any time before submitting to continue an unfinished online application, and can upload further documents through the same login once they advance a stage.
The Foundation informs every applicant by email about the result of each stage, and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting.

No file size limit, accepted file-type list, translation rule, certification rule or document-expiry rule is published on the pages read. The documents checklist PDF and the reference-writing guidance are published as separate files and were not downloaded.
official_details.selection_notes: The procedure has five published steps. Step 1: complete the online application form; FES staff check it against formal and substantive criteria, and within two to four weeks of receipt the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references. Step 2: submit documents and references; the file is reviewed and the applicant receives either a rejection or notification that the application has been passed to a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. Step 3: the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent, from which a Gutachten is produced and attached to the file; the applicant then receives either a rejection or notification that the file has gone to a member of the selection committee. Step 4: the second selection interview with a person from the selection committee, producing a further Gutachten attached to the file and tabled at the committee's meeting. Step 5: decision by the selection committee, which meets eight to ten times a year; once both Gutachten are available the application is presented in detail to the committee at the relevant meeting and the members decide on admission to the funding programme. The Foundation informs the applicant of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting, whether that is an offer or a rejection, and states that the whole process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
application_steps: Apply early. The Foundation states the best time to apply is as early as possible, because it wants scholarship holders to benefit from the scholarship for as long as possible, and the deadlines are listed per programme.

Check your degree-stage window. Master's: before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May). Bachelor, Diplom, Magister, Staatsexamen: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study. Medicine: after the fourth semester or after the Physikum, to the end of the sixth semester.

Complete the online application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German, covering general personal information, professional and family background, your motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and your socio-political engagement.
Submit the form. FES staff check it against the formal and substantive criteria.
Wait two to four weeks. You will receive either a rejection or an email requesting your documents and references.

If invited, submit within the stated windows: three weeks for the documents and up to six weeks for the references. Documents: a detailed CV covering your previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate and other evidence; and a detailed letter of motivation. References: two Gutachten from university lecturers.
Consult the Foundation's published Grundförderung document and reference checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 for the full required list for this programme.
Use your FES login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login to upload further documents when you advance to the next stage. FES confirms receipt of the documents.
If the file passes, attend the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. A Gutachten is produced and attached to your file.
If you advance, attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee. A second Gutachten is produced.
If you have travelled for an interview, submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung to claim reimbursement of your travel costs.

Await the decision. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and you will be informed by email at the latest one week after the meeting, whether the outcome is an offer or a rejection. The full process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits directly. The online application form, the documents and the references are all submitted by the applicant to the Foundation, with no institutional nomination and no employer or university acting as an intermediary.
Applications may be submitted formally from Germany or from abroad: 'Bewerbungen sind formell sowohl aus Deutschland als auch aus dem Ausland möglich.'

The two Gutachten must be written by university lecturers, or by teachers for first-year students, and submitted by the applicant with the document package within the stated six-week window. The Foundation publishes guidance on preparing the references separately.
After the first stage, further documents are uploaded by the applicant through the Foundation's own application login.
The Foundation's contact addresses for Auslandsförderung are published for questions, not as a submission channel; submission is through the online system.
official_details.application_portal: The Foundation's online application system at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A (the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen form), with applicant login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login.
arrival_rules: The applicant must already be living in Germany and studying at a German university at the time of application, and applications may formally be submitted from Germany or from abroad. Consequently there is no arrival provision: the applicant is already in Germany when applying.
No arrival date, latest-arrival rule, visa support arrangement or relocation funding is published. Study abroad programmes outside the EU and short-term stays abroad are not funded.
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and the Foundation's stage-two document request includes the enrolment certificate.
timeline_rules: The best time to apply is as early as possible, because the Foundation wants scholarship holders to benefit for as long as possible.

Application windows by degree stage: Master's, before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May); Bachelor, Diplom, Magister and Staatsexamen, after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study (English page: until three semesters before finishing the standard period of study, so by the end of the 3rd semester on a six-semester programme or the end of the 4th semester on a seven-semester programme); medicine, after the fourth semester or after the Physikum to the end of the sixth semester. The Foundation's English page also states diploma, magister and state examination by the end of the 6th semester.

There is no single annual closing date: applications are accepted on a rolling basis within the stage-specific windows, which is why the record's deadline_date is only meaningful as the 30 November master's-stage date.
Step 1 to first outcome: within two to four weeks of receiving the online application, the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references.
Step 2: three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, with a receipt confirmation on arrival.
The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year, and the applicant is informed of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting.
Total elapsed time from application to decision: three to seven months.
The Foundation informs all applicants by email about the result of each individual stage.
Applicants who have not yet submitted their online application can log in at any time and continue editing it.
official_application_route: Complete the online application form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German.
The form is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria, and a decision or a document request follows within two to four weeks.

On invitation, submit the document package and two academic references through the Foundation's application login within three weeks for documents and up to six weeks for references, using the Grundförderung checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 as the governing list.
Attend the first selection interview with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent if invited.
Attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee if shortlisted.
Submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung if you have incurred interview travel costs.

The decision is communicated by email at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting. The Foundation does not publish a postal submission route for the Grundförderung; the online system is the route.

important_advice_for_students: You must already be enrolled at a German university when you apply. This is the first gate, and it is not waivable — an offer of admission is not enough, enrolment is. Plan around being in Germany before the window closes.

German is mandatory, not optional. B2 is the level the Foundation states it accepts, and it accepts it without a certificate, but the application must still be written and submitted in German. Even if you study in English, you must prove German.

Check your degree-stage window before anything else. The windows are different for Master's, Bachelor, and medicine, and they are expressed relative to your semester count rather than as a calendar date. Applying in the wrong window is the most likely reason for an automatic rejection.

Check the funding-exclusion list against your course. A two-semester Master's, medical study up to the Physikum, any doctoral or postdoc stage, a research visit, physiotherapy or psychotherapy training, part-time study, and study outside the EU are all excluded. If your programme is short or part-time, this is the wrong scheme.
A second degree or a language course is not funded unless you already hold an FES scholarship. If you are planning to change course, check whether the new course would be a second degree.
Have your first graded performance records in hand before you apply. They are a stated prerequisite, and Bachelor's students must submit them.

Do the two academic references early. You have three weeks for documents but up to six weeks for the references, so the references are the long pole. University lecturers, not teachers, write them unless you are a first-year student.

Write the civic engagement part seriously. Soci-political commitment and identifying with the values of social democracy are two of the three baseline yes/no questions, and the Foundation looks for students who identify with social democracy and treat volunteering as self-evident.

Play to the Foundation's published priority groups if any apply to you: first in your family to study, migration background, women, universities of applied sciences, STEM. The Foundation states it gives particular weight to these applications.

Budget for what is not covered. The published package is 992 Euro per month plus health insurance costs, with an additional amount for children. Tuition and semester fees at your institution are not listed as covered. Ask your university what the semester contribution is and keep it in your own budget.

Watch the offset rule. The Foundation's English page states that any income exceeding 400 Euro per month is credited against the scholarship, so part-time earnings above that threshold reduce your stipend.
Claim interview travel costs if you have them. The Foundation reimburses travel costs for applicants invited to a selection interview, using its own form. Submit it.

Allow three to seven months. The process runs from the online form through a document request, two interviews with two separate Gutachten, and a committee meeting, and the committee only sits eight to ten times a year.

Talk to a scholarship ambassador before you apply. The Foundation points applicants to its stipendien-botschafter:innen for questions and for encouragement before applying, and these are former holders who answer questions they would rather answer themselves.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the current semester contribution fee at my institution, and does the university offer any waiver for scholarship holders? The Foundation does not publish that it pays it.
What health insurance plan will I be enrolled in, and does its cost vary with my age, marital status or dependants? The Foundation says it covers health insurance costs but publishes no figure.
What counts as the 'first graded performance records' required at application, and does my university issue them in a form I can upload directly?
Does my university offer a thesis supervisor or academic mentor willing to write a Gutachten, and how long do they take?
What is the standard period of study for my programme, so that I can calculate the three-semester application window correctly?
Is there a German course requirement attached to my programme that I should start now, given that applications must be submitted in German?
Does my institution have a scholarship-holder network or working group that FES scholarship holders join, and what does it expect of me in terms of time?
How much do the 18 thematic working groups and the political education seminars take in study time, on top of my coursework?
Is my course one of the excluded categories by another name — for example is it run part-time, is it a two-semester Master's, or is it a research stay rather than a degree programme?
What is the Foundation's offset calculation in practice if I have part-time income, and over what period is it assessed?
How do I apply for the additional amount for scholarship holders with children, and what is the current monthly figure?
Can I change my host institution or my subject after being awarded, and does that affect the stipend?

verification.source_conflict_rule: The programme page for Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen governs this specific scheme's scope, package and degree-stage windows, and the online application page governs the procedure, document list and deadlines. The Foundation's English 'Information in English' page is a cross-programme summary covering all FES schemes; where it differs from the programme page, the programme-specific German page governs, and every difference is recorded in institution_check_required rather than silently resolved. Where the English page is the only source for a rule, such as the 400 € income offset, it is cited explicitly as the English page.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The cycle is continuous and the windows are semester-relative rather than calendar-anchored, so there is no single annual date to go stale; what does change is the stipend rate, the family or children's allowance, the fee schedule at German institutions and the exclusion list. All of these must be re-read each academic cycle before an applicant budgets, and the selection committee's eight-to-ten-meetings-per-year cadence means a rejection is not final until a specific meeting date has passed.

records.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

records.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.

records.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.
records.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. The award cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research contract or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity. A PhD defended after December 2026 is not eligible. If the doctoral degree certificate has not yet been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is accepted. For researchers who obtained their PhD more than five years ago, the eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child, or by the actual duration of maternity leave, on submission of supporting documents noted in the application file. Only projects with a genuine integrated 'One Health' approach qualify under the human, animal and environmental health theme; projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible.

records.application_period: Call opened 16 July 2026 at 09:00 CEST. Step 1 submission and registration closes 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time. Step 1 results are notified mid-February 2027; step 2 runs from end February 2027 (template and IRIS opening) with submission closing end March 2027; selected projects are announced July 2027.
records.description: The AAPG is the ANR's main competitive call and it funds project-based research in every scientific field, including recruitment of doctoral students (contrats doctoraux) and young researchers on successful projects. records.duration: 12 to 24 months

records.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.
records.best_fit: Researchers who received a PhD within the past six years (maternity and parental leave time is subtracted) and who can secure a host researcher and host institution in Japan before applying.
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan who obtained a doctoral degree on or after April 2 of the year six years before the fiscal year, or who are expected to hold a PhD by the fellowship start date.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

As of April 1 of the fiscal year, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after April 2, six years prior to the fiscal year), or who are expected to receive a Ph.D. by the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks of leave counted as one month)

records.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.

records.name: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Graduate Degree Programs (Master's and Doctoral)
records.official_source: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Republic of Korea
records.region: South Korea (applicants: applicants and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship; developing countries for the R-GKS track)
records.duration: Master's degree 2 years, doctoral degree 3 years, following 1 year of Korean language training
records.deadline: Annual cycle: NIIED announcement in February, application submission February to March, review April to June, final results in June. No specific day-level deadline is published on this page; applicants must apply through the Korean Embassy or consulate in their country of residence, which sets its own deadline.
records.application_period: Announcement by NIIED in February, application submission February to March, screening and selection April to June, final results in June. The studyinkorea 'Apply for the GKS' button currently reports that it is not the application period, so the 2026 cycle is closed and the next window is the February-March 2027 cycle.
records.description: The GKS graduate degree track invites international students to study for a master's or doctoral degree at a designated Korean university. Published scholarship benefits are airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition, and monthly allowances. The programme covers Korean language training of one year before the degree study, with a two-year master's or three-year doctoral duration. Selection quota is approximately 2,000 places for graduate study, split across Embassy Track and University Track with specialisations including R&D and Global Network.
records.best_fit: International master's or doctoral applicants with a bachelor's or master's degree and at least an 80% average GPA from their most recent academic programme, applying through their Korean embassy or directly to a GKS-designated university.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under 40, hold non-Korean citizenship along with both parents, have graduated with a bachelor's or master's degree, and have an average GPA of at least 80% from their most recent academic programme.
eligibility: Nationality: the applicant and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship
Age: must be under 40 years of age
Level of education: must have graduated with a bachelor's or master's degree
GPA: must have an average GPA of at least 80% from the most recent academic program
R&D specialisation is available only for Master's and Doctoral programs; Global Network is master's degree only and delivered without Korean language training

records.region: South Korea (applicants: non-Korean nationals from a published list of Asian, American, European and African countries, including Japan)
records.duration: Master's: full tuition for 4 semesters and living expenses for 22 months. Doctoral or integrated master's and doctoral: full tuition for 6 semesters and living expenses for 36 months.

records.description: The POSCO TJ Park Foundation awards a scholarship to international students admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school and recommended by that institution. Benefits published are full tuition, living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month, a one-time settlement fee of KRW 1,000,000, National Health Insurance premium, Korean language education support, and cultural programmes. Master's students receive full tuition for 4 semesters and living expenses for 22 months; doctoral and integrated master's and doctoral students receive full tuition for 6 semesters and living expenses for 36 months. Twenty students are selected per year, subject to change.

records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold or expect to hold a bachelor's degree, hold non-Korean nationality, be admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school, and be recommended by that institution.

records.name: Apoyo Complementario SECIHTI-OEA 2026
records.official_source: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación (Secihti) and Organización de los Estados Americanos (OAS)
records.region: Mexico (beneficiaries must be nationals of OAS Member States other than Mexico)
records.deadline: Fecha de cierre del proceso: 30 de noviembre de 2026
records.application_period: Publicación de la convocatoria: 28 de agosto de 2026. Secihti sends the compliant list to the OAS on 28 August 2026; award committee deliberates 3 September 2026; direct notification 4-10 September 2026; formalisation 7-18 September 2026; process closes 30 November 2026.
records.description: A complementary support awarded jointly by the OAS and Mexico's Secihti to students who already hold a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in Mexico. The OAS contribution is a single payment of USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, and the number of supports depends on OAS funds. Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. The call does not establish tuition, travel or full living-cost coverage, so this is not full funding.
records.best_fit: Non-Mexican nationals of OAS Member States who are already current holders of a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in one of the listed STEM, health, biotechnology or agricultural sciences areas in Mexico.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must already be current Secihti National Scholarship holders admitted and enrolled in a full-time postgraduate programme in a listed subject area, and be nationals of an OAS Member State other than Mexico.
eligibility: Declarar en su perfil único tener la nacionalidad de alguno de los Estados Miembros de la OEA, con excepción de México.

Haber obtenido una Beca Secihti Nacional in one of the six named calls: Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado programas elegibles 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Humanidades y Ciencias de la Conducta 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Entidades Federativas con Mayor Rezago Social 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado para Especialidades en Áreas de la Salud 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en programas que pertenezcan a las áreas de Físico-Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías y Desarrollo Tecnológico 2025 segundo periodo; or Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado 2026, término de referencia A, programas elegibles escolarizados, primer periodo.
Ser persona becaria nacional vigente en un programa de posgrado escolarizado.

Estar admitido e inscrito en las áreas de Física, Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías, Medicina y Ciencias de la Salud (a excepción de la formación de especialidades y subespecialidades médicas), Biotecnología y Ciencias Agropecuarias.
coverage: OAS: single contribution of USD 1,200 for gastos de instalación (settling-in expenses) in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate of the day OAS deposits to the beneficiary's bank account.
Secihti: monthly economic support according to the 'Tabulador de Becas Nacionales 2026'.
Secihti: medical service provided by ISSSTE, on registering as a beneficiary under ISSSTE rules.
benefits: The OAS portion is explicitly stated to be independent from the scholarship granted by Secihti.
requirements: The beneficiary must send the information and documentation that the OAS requests for formalisation and disbursement, on time and in full.

Under article 17-A of the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo, a failure to send that information triggers a single emailed prevención with a term of no fewer than five business days; if it is not corrected, the support may be cancelled and reassigned.
application_method: There is no public application form for new applicants: participation requires already being a current national scholarship holder selected under one of the calls listed in the eligibility section.
Secihti validates the applications of persons who were beneficiaries under the listed calls and sends the compliant list to the OAS on 28 August 2026.
The OAS Award Committee deliberates on 3 September 2026 and Secihti and the OAS notify selected students directly between 4 and 10 September 2026.
Results of the assigned applications are published on the OAS website and notified by email from both Secihti and the OAS.
Formalisation is carried out by signing the corresponding instrument between the OAS and the selected beneficiary.
Disbursement is made once the support has been formalised, following the timetable and procedure the OAS communicates by email.

records.duration: 4 months (online course running 16 March - 22 June 2027)

records.description: The GS/OAS and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile fund USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 total course fee for a 4-month online certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global 2026), focused on SDG 13 climate action. The selected candidate remains responsible for USD 400 of the course fee, plus study materials or equipment, internet access, and any additional fees not included in the offer. Living costs, travel and insurance are not addressed at all in the announcement, so this is not full funding and there is no stipend to live on.
records.best_fit: Young professionals from OAS Member States other than Chile who have a business management background, a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship, and can commit about 4.5 hours a week in English to a fully online course.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of an active OAS Member State other than Chile, be proficient in English, have a strong business management background, and commit to paying the remaining USD 400 course fee.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.
Have a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship.
Innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience is especially encouraged, or one that addresses a need in the market.
Can 'think outside the box,' exhibit critical thinking skills, and have a quest for discovery or investigative learning.
Demonstrate the ability to lead and inspire others.
Be a young professional who has an idea to develop, or is in the process of developing a small or medium enterprise in an active OAS member state.
Have a strong background in business management.
Be proficient in English.
Commit to at least 4.5 hours a week to the course over a one-semester period consisting of synchronous (live) and asynchronous content.
Have access to a computer with a reliable Internet connection, with appropriate video and audio functions.
Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.
coverage: USD 3,400 of the total course fee, contributed jointly by the GS/OAS and the University, out of a total cost of USD 3,800.
Access to the 100% online course delivered through UDD's Canvas platform.
A formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo on successful completion of the program.

Connection with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile.
requirements: Submit a complete application through the online application link, including all supporting documents.
Cover the remaining USD 400 course fee to the UDD.
The scholarship will be formally awarded only after selected recipients sign an OAS Acceptance Form agreeing to its terms and conditions.

Comply with all academic guidelines requested by UDD and submit updates to those guidelines and requirements made by UDD's academic authorities.
records.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570+ (paper), 230+ (computer), or 79+ (internet-based/IBT); or IELTS 6.5 or equivalent.
application_method: Prepare all supporting documents combined into one single PDF file not exceeding 5 MB, in English or with an official English translation.
Complete the OAS online scholarship application, noting that the system permits only one document upload.
Submit the complete application package with all supporting documents via the OAS link no later than 31 January 2027.
If pre-selected, respond to the email contact and take part in an interview with the scholarship selection committee in English, if necessary.
If finally selected, sign the formal OAS acceptance form after being contacted by email with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions.
records.selection_notes: A specialized OAS and UDD committee selects the recipients. Elements considered in awarding the scholarships are geographic distribution of the candidates, the applicant's profile including education and project outline and recommendation, the applicant's potential impact on completion of the course, and gender distribution. A selection committee pre-selects participants on that profile; pre-selected participants may be interviewed in English. Results are published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027, and unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
records.notes: This is a fee-reduction award, not a living stipend: the scholarship covers USD 3,400 of a USD 3,800 course fee and the recipient must find USD 400 plus study materials, equipment and internet access themselves. No living cost, travel or health insurance funding is published, so applicants must not budget this as full funding. Not eligible: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff and their immediate family, GS/OAS consultants, and permanent OAS staff and their immediate family. The recipient may decline the scholarship before the program start date without financial penalty, but declining after that date without proof of force majeure may require repayment of all funds awarded. The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel this scholarship announcement at any time during the process.

application_method: Step 1: Follow the admission process for the chosen programme directly with the institution, submitting all documentation the institution requires, and pay the admission fee.

Step 2: Once admitted and in receipt of the institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion), the applicant is automatically considered a candidate for the OAS-UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico scholarship; there is no separate scholarship application form.
Step 3: UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS form a specialised committee to select the scholarship holders.
Step 4: Await publication of results at www.oea.org/becas, announced from November 2026 for the 2a convocatoria.

records.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit program expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years

records.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
records.best_fit: Graduate students in science, engineering, mathematics and related fields who hold a relevant bachelor's (Master's entry) or relevant master's (Ph.D. entry) degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 and clear research interests.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject for Master's entry or a relevant master's degree for Ph.D. entry, be at least 18 years old on entry, hold a minimum 3.0/4.0 GPA, and demonstrate English proficiency.
eligibility: Bachelors degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Master's programs

Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry
Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent); typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5
Evidence of proficiency in the English language
coverage: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year)
Monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 for Ph.D. students)
Base accommodation (shared accommodation for single students; 2-bed accommodation for married students)
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs
benefits: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee
Relocation assistance covers each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation
Over 90% of admitted students receive full tuition support, a monthly stipend, housing, medical coverage and relocation assistance
requirements: Submit an application through the KAUST online application portal before the published round deadline
Provide contact details of 3 referees with academic or professional email addresses; personal email addresses are not accepted
Provide an official English language test score if available
Provide a clear, unobscured copy of the passport page showing picture and personal details (Saudi applicants may provide a national ID card)
All supporting documents, including academic transcripts, must be in English
If your official transcript is not in English, upload both the original transcript in the native language and a certified English translation
A statement of purpose of approximately 750 words
GRE or PGAT scores may be submitted but are not a compulsory requirement
records.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores valid for two years from the test date.
application_method: Log into the KAUST application portal and submit the application before the published round deadline
Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score and passport page as part of the online application
Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically
Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area
Await the decision notification by email within the published notification window for the round
records.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
records.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.

referee_tracking.instructions: Applicants are normally expected to nominate academic referees. Provide an academic email address, not a personal one. The referee is asked to describe how they know your work, give comparative statements such as top 1% of class or best in past five years, and give insight into your research ability. records.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.

records.notes: M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is NOT guaranteed for all admitted students; students without a funding source are classified as fee-paying. records.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.

records.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.

records.region: Netherlands (applicants from outside the European Economic Area)
records.deadline: The application for the academic year 2026-2027 opened on 1 November 2025. Please check the website of the institution you want to apply to for the specific deadline(s).

The central page published the 2026-2027 opening date of 1 November 2025 and had not yet published a 2027-2028 opening date when checked.
records.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.
records.best_fit: Non-EEA nationals applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the listed participating Dutch research universities or universities of applied sciences who can fund the remainder of tuition and living costs themselves.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of non-EEA nationality, be applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution, meet that institution's own requirements, and not hold a degree from a Dutch education institution.
eligibility: Your nationality is non-EEA.
You are applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.
You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice. You can find these on the website of the institution.
You do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands.
Radboud University: You must not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons.

Radboud University: You must have (will obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and did not receive any previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided that they are part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands).
Radboud University: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice.
Radboud University: You must be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands.
Utrecht University: You must not be eligible for statutory tuition fees.

Utrecht University: You must never have been enrolled at an educational institution in the Netherlands (if you only took part in an exchange programme in the Netherlands, this does not make you ineligible).
coverage: A one-off grant of € 5,000 paid in the first year of studies (Study in NL and Radboud University figures).
Nothing else. Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship; Radboud University states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
benefits: At Radboud University the NL Scholarship is always combined with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP): applicants must also apply for the RSP, and can be awarded both or just the RSP, never the NLS alone.
Utrecht University publishes three award tiers rather than one: €5,000, €10,000 and €15,000, all paid in the first year of studies even for a two-year programme.
Nuffic states the programme is made available jointly with 47 Dutch higher education institutions, which will grant scholarships to 2,112 students per academic year.
requirements: Apply for an NL Scholarship-eligible programme at a participating institution and meet that institution's admission and scholarship requirements.
Utrecht University: your application must be submitted before 1 February, 23:59 CET; the application portal closes at that time and selection only starts after the deadline.
Utrecht University: results are aimed to be published by mid-April.

Utrecht University: you must demonstrate you can cover the remaining costs by completing the Statement of Financial Resources, showing a realistic plan covering the full nominal duration of the Master's programme.

Radboud University: your OSIRIS application must be submitted by 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest, and must be complete by 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest; incomplete applications will not be considered for scholarship selection.
Radboud University: proof of English proficiency should be handed in before the 14 February 2027 deadline.
Radboud University: the decision is communicated around mid-April 2027 (date subject to change).
Nuffic operates an integrity Code of Conduct; the programme may not be involved in financial misconduct, tax or social security default, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct.
application_method: Choose a participating Dutch institution and an NL Scholarship-eligible programme (not every programme participates).
Apply for admission to that programme through the institution's own application system.
Radboud University: indicate during the OSIRIS application procedure for a Master's programme that you wish to apply for an NL Scholarship.

Utrecht University: submit the application for an NL Scholarship-eligible MA programme, log in to your OSIRIS Online Application account, locate 'NL Scholarship' under your dashboard, click 'View/Edit' for the scholarship linked to your chosen programme, open the application form, answer all required questions and submit.
Meet your institution's published deadline and completeness deadline.
Upload all required documents, including the institutional financial-plans form where required.
Await the selection outcome, published by the institution after its deadline.
records.selection_notes: Utrecht University assesses applications on the academic background shown in the master's programme application, the motivation explaining the relevance of the time in the Netherlands and at Utrecht University to future goals, and the quality and feasibility of the financial plan. Radboud University assesses on academic excellence (outstanding study results, relevance of the previous degree to the programme, ranking of the university where previous degrees were obtained) and ambition (quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise shown by achievements, life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering), with each faculty considering its own applicants individually. Admission to the programme and selection for the scholarship are two separate processes.
records.notes: This is not full funding and should never be budgeted as such: Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship and Radboud University states explicitly that the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. At Radboud University the award is limited to one year and can only be received once. The programme was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship in June 2023, so older material under the old name may be out of date. Selection for the scholarship is separate from admission to the programme — an admission offer does not imply a scholarship. Utrecht University requires applicants to prove they can cover the full remaining cost of the programme.

records.description: The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship supporting early career scientists from underrepresented backgrounds to establish research in a UK institution. Applicants can apply for up to £703,800 over four years, covering a contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs (at 80%), directly allocated costs (at 80%), and research expenses (at 100%). Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants can be requested in addition to the grant cap. The scheme is funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Royal Society charitable funds, with a variant funding research directly relevant to dementia in partnership with the Alzheimer's Society.

records.eligibility_summary: Self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, have a UK connection (national, education or a UK postdoc position), hold or be completing a PhD with less than 24 months postdoctoral experience, and work within the Royal Society's natural sciences remit.
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible.
Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.

records.name: Humboldt Research Fellowship
records.region: Germany (host research institution)
records.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
records.deadline: Rolling in three calls per year, each opening approximately eight months before the selection meeting and closing when 800 applications are received. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 for the July 2027 selection meeting, with the earliest possible fellowship start in September 2027. The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications and no new applications can be created.
records.application_period: Three calls per year: opened 15 March 2026 (selection meeting November 2026, earliest start February 2027), 15 July 2026 (selection meeting March 2027, earliest start May 2027), and next on 15 November 2026 (selection meeting July 2027, earliest start September 2027). Each call closes automatically once 800 applications are received.
records.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
records.best_fit: Non-German postdoctoral researchers who completed their doctorate within the last four years (or experienced researchers within twelve years) and need a 6-24 month research stay in Germany.
records.eligibility_summary: Non-German national with a doctorate completed within the last four years (postdoc track) or twelve years (experienced researcher track), no more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying, with a German host providing a mentoring agreement and a confirmation of research facilities.
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).
