requirements: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only
You may only submit your application once you have uploaded all required documents in the application form
Two expert reviews must be uploaded in a protected area by the expert reviewers personally; you can only submit once these have been uploaded if the portal is open at that time
Your host will receive a link to upload a host's statement and mentoring agreement; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents
Applications that fail to include important documents or information, or that diverge substantially from the specifications, will be formally rejected without further review
records.english_requirement: Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise, good knowledge of English will suffice. No language certificate is required if English or German is your native language. An English language certificate is not required if you have worked in an English-speaking country for several years.
application_method: Wait for an open call; the current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications and the next opens 15 November 2026
Register in the application portal and complete the application form
Upload the required applicant documents (CV, research outline, publication lists, key publications, doctoral certificate)

Submit the application; the application is automatically forwarded to your host, who uploads the host's statement and mentoring agreement
The application is only received by the Foundation once all documents, including the host's, have been submitted
records.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.
records.notes: The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications, so no new applications can be created at present; the next call opens on 15 November 2026. Applicants who have already started an application can save and continue working on it but cannot submit until the next application round opens. Applications are forwarded to the Foundation only after the host has uploaded their documents, so the host's speed determines your effective submission. Applicant who has already worked in Germany for 12 months or more should look for a new academic environment; applications involving returning to the doctoral supervisor or mentor of a longer postdoctoral stay are generally rejected. Individuals with whom you are in a close personal or familial relationship cannot be selected as hosts. In the case of unanimously rejected applications you must wait a minimum of 18 months before re-applying. Decisions cannot be appealed.

eligibility: Postdocs: doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - completed during the last four years.

Experienced researchers: doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - completed during the last twelve years, with an extensive publication record including important papers where you acted as thematic lead, and a leadership role commensurate with your career level.

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. German citizens or educational residents may apply only with more than ten years living and working abroad long-term, or more than five years abroad with a strong connection to the current country of residence.
You may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.
A German host must provide a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and must compile a detailed review.
Two expert reviews: for postdocs, the doctoral supervisor and one other researcher, outside of your institute if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: good knowledge of German if necessary for the research, otherwise good knowledge of English.
You may not apply if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).

records.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
records.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
records.funding_period: up to, over the award duration (usually 5 years)
records.eligibility_summary: Early-career researcher with a passed PhD viva or at least four years' equivalent research experience, no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at least 80% of research time on the project, based at an eligible administering organisation.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
coverage: Total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant, determined by the administering organisation, including basic salary, employer contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental salary progression and locally recognised allowances
Up to £400,000 for research expenses
Overheads, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit; total overhead cost should not be more than 20% of direct research costs
Overseas allowances and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit
Adjustment support including assistive technology and support staff, which does not count towards the £400,000 limit
Visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, their partner and dependent children, plus Immigration Health Surcharge costs if in the UK six months or more
Relocation allowance of up to £1,000 to cover personal removal costs
Staff salaries up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post
Conference attendance contributions: £2,000 a year for the grantholder and £1,000 each a year for research and technical staff, plus accredited carbon credits to mitigate emissions
Caring responsibility costs at conferences up to £1,000 per person per conference, subject to the stated conditions

Continuing professional development and professional skills training up to £500 a year per person, and research skills training, for staff in posts of 12 months or more working on the grant at 50% FTE or more
Materials and consumables, animals, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer equipment, and access charges for shared equipment, facilities or services
benefits: If, after two or more years from the activation date, your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes your salary, you can keep the salary element of the award to use towards your remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa
The award may be held on a part-time basis, with the duration extended to reflect this; the application must still be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent
Access to Wellcome's global talent, mentoring and community networks

records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
records.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.

official_details.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award provides funding for early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity. Through innovative projects they will deliver shifts in understanding related to human life, health and wellbeing, and by the end of the award they will be ready to lead their own independent research programme. The award funds the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant plus up to £400,000 for research expenses, with certain costs outside the £400,000 limit.

alerts.message: If your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract including your salary two or more years after activation, you can keep the salary element to spend on remaining research costs.
Staff salaries are capped at the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, with extra possible only for specialist technical experts or disability support. No studentships are available on this award.

submission_workflow: Run the self-assessment tool and confirm career-stage eligibility
Confirm the research fits the Discovery Research remit

Complete and submit the application in Wellcome Funding
Track the decision and note the resubmission limit before deciding whether to re-apply

referee_tracking.instructions: An individual at your administering organisation holding an established post or honorary academic appointment for the duration of the award. They must guarantee space and resources from the start date to the end date, confirm the research environment will support the project, and confirm workload expectations (no more than 20% of your time on non-research activities, up to 40% clinical duties in a clinical craft speciality). Sponsors are not paid for their input.

Should have a track record in training and mentorship and support you to manage your application, develop your research career, progress your personal development, and manage processes and regulations at the administering organisation. Does not need to be based at the administering organisation and is not paid. Your sponsor can also be your mentor.

If you plan to work for more than three months outside your administering organisation, you must also have an additional sponsor at that location who must guarantee the space and resources you will need during your visit.

Collaborators support delivery but do not lead a component, do not have to meet eligibility requirements, cannot receive a salary or compensation, and are not required to give a minimum research time commitment.

post_award_requirements: Deliver the project with at least 80% of your research time committed to it
Report on progress and expenditure through your administering organisation under Wellcome's grant conditions
Comply with Wellcome's environmental sustainability funding policy, including considering lower-carbon travel and mitigating travel emissions where requested
Manage staff and equipment within the costed award duration; the award is not renewable

For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
records.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
records.best_fit: Nationals of listed developing countries who hold a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline, have at least three years of paid development-related work experience acquired within the past six years, and can first secure unconditional admission (except funding) to one of only 44 participating master's programmes outside their country of citizenship and residence.
records.funding_period: per trip (published travel allowance only; the monthly subsistence allowance amount is not published)
records.eligibility_summary: National of a listed World Bank developing country with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the application deadline, at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, and unconditional admission (except funding) to a JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme outside their country of citizenship and residence.
eligibility: Be a national of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Be in good health
Hold a bachelor's (or equivalent) degree earned at least 3 years prior to the Application Deadline date

Be employed in development-related work in a paid full-time position at the time of submitting the scholarship application, with at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past 6 years from the date of the application deadline

On or before the scholarship application deadline date, be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) for the upcoming academic year to at least one of the JJ/WBGSP participating master's programs located outside of the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence listed at the time the call for scholarship applications opens; the letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

Not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Individuals who have previously been offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but declined it, or who previously received a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but did not graduate, are not eligible to apply again
Exception: applicants from a country on the list of Fragile and Conflict States in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have their limited employment opportunities taken into consideration
coverage: Tuition for the graduate program
Cost of basic medical insurance obtained through the university

Monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus during the scholarship period (accommodations, food, books); amount varies by host country and is not published on the programme page
Economy class air travel between the home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately after the scholarship period
US$600 travel allowance for each trip
benefits: The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Participation in the JJ/WBGSP alumni community of more than 7,000 mid-career professionals from 160 developing countries and Japan
requirements: Must already hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened
The letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates who are admitted unconditionally (except for finance) to a participating master's program and shortlisted as eligible JJ/WBGSP applicants by the participating university
All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions; they will not change during an open call for applications
application_method: Choose a target from the published list of participating master's programs for the relevant application window
Apply directly to that university and satisfy its own admission requirements and internal deadlines
Be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to the participating master's program
Ask the university whether you meet both conditions: unconditional admission and shortlisting as an eligible JJ/WBGSP applicant
Once the university shortlists you, it communicates the link to the JJ/WBGSP application form
Upload the admission letter and submit the JJ/WBGSP application within the application window
records.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
records.notes: Not eligible if admitted to a non-participating programme: the World Bank states explicitly that if you are not admitted to one of the participating master's programs you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP scholarship in 2027. The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you hold another award you must send those documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree. Declining an earlier offer, or receiving the scholarship and failing to graduate, permanently bars reapplication. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 developing-country-national cycle is live.

official_details.description: The JJ/WBGSP is open to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts who are applying to a master's degree program in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, JJ/WBGSP offers scholarships for 44 Participating Master's Programs in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan in key areas of development, including economic policy management, tax policy, and infrastructure management. A JJ/WBGSP scholarship provides tuition, a monthly living stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance, and travel allowance.

records.name: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
records.official_source: UNESCO, funded by the Government of Japan under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources
records.region: Japan (host country). Applicants must be nationals of invited Member States or Associate Members: Africa (47 Member States), Arab States (1 Member State: Bahrain), Asia and the Pacific (17 Member States and 2 Associate Members), Latin America and the Caribbean (16 Member States and 7 Associate Members), and Europe (2 Member States: Turkiye and Ukraine).
records.duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months
records.deadline: Deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. Letters of nomination and all application documents must reach UNESCO from the National Commissions no later than 15 October 2026, and candidates must submit to their own National Commission at least 2 weeks before the required deadline.
records.application_period: Cycle 2026 call is open (page last updated 28 September 2026, stating the application for the Cycle 2026 is open and the deadline is now extended to 15 October 2026). Because the National Commission needs at least two weeks, the practical national deadline falls around 1 October 2026. Fellowship period in Japan from February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027.
records.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.
records.program_type: UN agency research fellowship (UN and government co-sponsored)
records.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under who hold at least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in a field relevant to the proposed research, come from an invited Member State or Associate Member, already have acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, and are applying in one of the five listed research areas on heritage conservation, AI for natural resources and climate action, ethical and human-centred AI, AI for sustainable cities and infrastructure, or AI and education.
records.funding_period: one-time lump sum, up to the published ceiling
records.eligibility_summary: National of an invited Member State or Associate Member, aged no more than 40 at the time of application, holding at least a Master's degree or equivalent relevant to the proposed research, proficient in the language of instruction or supervision at the Japanese host institution, and already accepted by an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution.

coverage: International and domestic travel for the approved itinerary

The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. official_details.description: Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO's mandate. Under the 2026 cycle, UNESCO and the Government of Japan will award 10 fellowships to highly qualified young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye. The fellowships support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence, with particular attention to interdisciplinary research connecting these themes with social, ethical, governance and contextual dimensions. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. Since its establishment, the Programme has enabled 300 young researchers from 100 countries around the world to pursue postgraduate research.

records.region: Japan (applicants must be Japanese nationals). The graduate programme must be outside Japan, in a development-related field, and may be in a developing country where the scholar has secured employment.

records.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.
records.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)
records.best_fit: Japanese nationals with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline and at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, who are admitted unconditionally (except financing) to, or already enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan.
records.funding_period: per trip, paid twice (one $600 travel allowance each way; the monthly subsistence allowance amount is not published)

records.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
records.notes: The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you are notified of being a semi-finalist or are awarded, you must inform and document other scholarship funds to the Secretariat. After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries. The air travel benefit at the end of the scholarship period is conditional on having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, and the return ticket is to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment. The published US$600 is a per-trip travel allowance, not the award total. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 window is live.

records.name: UBC International Scholars Program
records.region: Canada
records.deadline: Applications for the September 2027 intake will open on October 5, 2026. The International Scholars Program application is due November 15.
records.application_period: Applications open October 5, 2026 and close November 15, 2026 for September 2027 entry; required transcripts/academic certificates and proof of English Language Admission Standard due January 31, 2027; video interviews January to March; results released on a rolling basis February to April, with awards confirmed by early to mid-April.
records.description: The UBC International Scholars Program is a need-and-merit award scheme for international students entering their first undergraduate degree directly from secondary school who could not pursue a UBC degree without meaningful financial help. One application puts an applicant into consideration for four award categories: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award, Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award, International Impact Award, and the Vantage One Excellence Award. UBC does not publish a standard award value for the programme on this page; only the Vantage One Excellence Award is described as ranging in value up to the full cost of an academic programme and living expenses.
records.best_fit: International students finishing high school who have all-As-level grades, strong community involvement, and can document a significant financial need.
records.eligibility_summary: International students entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school for a first undergraduate degree, with outstanding academics and demonstrable significant financial need.
eligibility: You are an international student who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit.
You are entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school.
Applicants for 2027 Winter session must have graduated from high school no earlier than June 2026.
You are applying for your first undergraduate degree.
You can prove a significant level of financial need. It would be impossible for you to pursue a UBC degree without meaningful financial help.
Your family is not able to afford a significant level of your educational costs and does not have access to external funding.
You meet UBC's admission requirements, including general and degree-specific requirements.
You demonstrate superior academic achievement (achieve all As or equivalent standard).
You meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard.

The following degrees are not eligible: Bachelor of Nursing degree (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions.
benefits: Participation in skill building workshops and retreats
Dedicated International Scholars Program advisors for academic, personal and career development
Option to participate in exchange and co-op
Access to learning opportunities and a community of Scholars from diverse countries and cultures
requirements: Submit a UBC Admissions application before starting the award application; the award application requests confirmation of UBC application submission.
Secure one nominator (guidance counsellor, principal, administrator, etc.) and one teacher referee, who must be different people.
Submit four essay questions of approximately 150-250 words.
Gather family financial information: annual income and expenses, family wealth and assets, dependents and annual school fees, sources of financial support.
Calculate family contributions and financial need using the UBC cost estimator.
Complete any required video interview if invited.
records.english_requirement: You must meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard by January 31, 2027. If you are required to take an English language test, UBC states you must complete the test early enough for UBC Admissions to receive your official test results by January 31. This page does not name a specific test or score.
application_method: Mid-September: decide on your academic program and campus.

Late September: discuss the nomination with your school and confirm the school can nominate you; a high school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver and one for UBC Okanagan.
Early October: apply for admission to UBC (required before the award application).
Early October: create your award application account and invite your nominator and teacher referee to complete their forms; you cannot complete your application until both forms are submitted.
Mid-October: complete the financial and essay sections of the award application.
By November 15: submit your completed award application.
By January 31: submit required documents, transcripts and proof of English Language Admission Standard.
January to March: complete a video interview if invited.
Check your email for updates between February and April.
records.selection_notes: UBC states it runs a financial assessment as part of evaluating applications, reviewing documents outlining family gross income, expenses and family assets. You will not be considered for merit-based awards if you apply to the International Scholars Program. Results are released on a rolling basis from February, and by early to mid-April UBC confirms whether an award was received.
records.notes: A high school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one student for UBC Okanagan, so school nomination capacity is a real constraint. Applicants who apply to the International Scholars Program are not considered for UBC's merit-based awards. The programme page publishes no standard award amount, so do not budget from an assumed figure. If you are applying for UBC Housing, UBC advises waiting until award decisions are released before applying for residence; the housing deadline is May 1.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your high school or nominating non-profit organisation can nominate you: up to two students for UBC Vancouver and one for UBC Okanagan.
Secure a nominator and a teacher referee who are two different people, and collect their email addresses now.
Complete your UBC Admissions application first; the award application is gated on it.
Assemble official financial documents covering family gross income, expenses, family assets, dependents, school fees and other funding sources.
Draft four essays of roughly 150-250 words well before November 15.
Book any required English language test so official results reach UBC Admissions by January 31, 2027.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the November 15 deadline, which UBC warns makes success less likely for applications started shortly before it.
Incomplete application: the award application cannot be submitted until both the nominator and teacher referee forms are complete.
Failing the superior academic achievement standard (all As or equivalent).
Being unable to document a significant level of financial need through official documents.
Applying to an excluded degree such as Bachelor of Nursing, Dental Hygiene or Medical Laboratory Science.
Study permit status that does not match the programme's requirement to be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit.
Missing the January 31, 2027 document deadline, which UBC states stops it from proceeding with the application.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The programme page publishes no award value and no statement of which expenses the awards cover, so the uncovered balance cannot be calculated from the official source.
UBC advises waiting for award decisions before applying for housing; the housing application deadline is May 1, so plan for a period where housing is unsecured.
document_audit: Transcripts or high school academic certificates must be submitted by January 31, 2027, not the date listed in the general 'Your UBC Application - Next Steps' email.
If transcripts or certificates are not available by January 31, submit them as soon as they are available.
Official English language test results must reach UBC Admissions by January 31, 2027.
Financial need documents must be official, covering family gross income, expenses and family assets.

Submit UBC Admissions application in early October.
Create the award application account and send referee invitations in early October.

referee_tracking.role: High school nominator (guidance counsellor, principal or administrator)
referee_tracking.instructions: Should be able to speak to your educational goals and your character. The school or registered non-profit submits the nomination; nominations for UBC Vancouver are capped at two students and for UBC Okanagan at one.
Must be someone familiar with you and your work in your chosen area of study, and must be a different person from your nominator. Their form must be submitted a few days before November 15.

post_award_requirements: Maintain eligibility by continuing study at UBC as an international student; UBC notes that changing citizenship status or tuition fee rate can affect award eligibility and may result in recovery of award funding.
Participate in skill building workshops and retreats as a Scholar.
Engage with the International Scholars Program advisors during the degree.
